title: QA↔SEC-001: Threat-Derived Test Cases + Security Test Execution Evidence
description: The Security Engineer provides security test requirements, threat-derived test cases mapped to STRIDE (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, Elevation of Privilege) in the Threat-Derived Test Case Schema format, penetration-test scope and methodology, security acceptance criteria, and the security baseline specification; the QA & Test Automation Engineer provides security test execution results with objective evidence and traceability, verification of security-defect fixes with regression evidence, security vulnerability findings (reported within 1 business day of discovery), and security-test coverage reports as input to the release security gate. Grounded in SECURITY_ENGINEER_SKILL §6.8 and QA_TEST_AUTOMATION_ENGINEER_SKILL §6.10. Security-relevant: this contract feeds the Security Engineer's release go/no-go (HG-01) and fires ESC-SEC — QA executes and reports; the Security Engineer owns all binding security decisions.

security_test_package.description: SEC→QA: test requirements, threat-derived (STRIDE) test cases, pen-test scope, acceptance criteria, baseline.

qa_security_evidence.description: QA→SEC: test execution results, defect-fix verification, vulnerability findings, coverage reports.

vulnerability_findings.description: Reported within 1 business day of discovery.

coverage_report_ref.description: Security-test coverage report — input to the release security gate.

x-macp.tier_rationale: Threat-derived test-case handoff and security-test execution are coordinated at machine speed, but the evidence feeds the Security Engineer's release security gate (HG-01, Tier-1) and any vulnerability finding is security-relevant. ESC-SEC applies — QA executes and reports; the Security Engineer owns the binding go/no-go and risk-acceptance decisions.
x-macp.cadence: TRIGGER + SLA_FROM_EVENT (security-test alignment at planning; threat-derived test-case handoff within 10 business days of a threat-model update / security ADR / post-incident review; QA acknowledges in 2 business days, executes automated cases in 5 / manual in 10 business days, reports in 1 business day; vulnerability findings reported within 1 business day; quarterly test-case review; release-gate security sign-off)
confirm_conditions: each threat-derived test case carries a STRIDE category and an execution type
QA test results carry a PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict with evidence and traceability to the test-case id
vulnerability findings carry a severity and were reported within 1 business day of discovery
the security-test coverage report is provided as input to the release security gate
reject_conditions: a discovered vulnerability not reported within 1 business day, or downgraded in severity (Honesty Over Polish §10.3; ESC-SEC)
a security test reported PASS without objective evidence / traceability to the threat-derived case
a release security sign-off inferred from coverage without the Security Engineer's binding go/no-go (bypasses HG-01)
counter_conditions: ALWAYS escalate ESC-SEC when a finding touches the security baseline or a security-relevant release — propose, do not auto-confirm; the Security Engineer decides
a threat-derived test case cannot be executed as written (ambiguous steps, missing prerequisites) — flag back to Security within 2 business days with specific blockers
